questions.stem: Which part of the current ServiceNow interface helps a user find applications and modules by typing part of a name?
options: The All menu with its filter
questions.explanation: The All menu in the unified navigation lists applications and modules and has a filter field.

questions.stem: What is a ServiceNow instance?
options: A dedicated deployment of the platform with its own application and database for one customer
A single table in the database
A browser session for one user
A scheduled job that refreshes data
questions.explanation: Each customer works in its own instance of the platform.

questions.stem: What is a Personal Developer Instance (PDI) mainly used for?
options: Learning and building on the platform outside production
Hosting a company's live production service
questions.explanation: A PDI is a free instance for learning and development, not for production.

questions.stem: A user opens the same few modules every day. What is the quickest way to reach them again?
options: Create a new table for them
Import them with a transform map
questions.explanation: Favorites keep shortcuts to frequently used pages.

questions.stem: Where does an administrator go to browse and install available applications on the instance?
questions.explanation: Application Manager lists applications that can be installed or updated.

questions.stem: A user rearranges the columns on their own incident list. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Personalizing changes a user's own view and does not alter the platform for everyone.

questions.stem: Which change is a customization rather than a personalization?
options: Adding a new field to the Incident table for all users
Choosing a different list column order for yourself
Collapsing a form section for yourself
Changing how your own time zone displays
questions.explanation: Adding a field changes the platform for everyone, so it is a customization.

questions.stem: Which role gives full administrative access to configure an instance?
questions.explanation: The admin role grants full administrative access.

questions.stem: What are system properties used for?
options: Storing settings that control how the instance behaves
questions.explanation: System properties hold configuration settings that affect instance behavior.

questions.stem: Which interface lets end users browse the catalog and knowledge without the full platform UI?
questions.explanation: Service Portal is a simplified interface for end users.

questions.stem: A user wants a list showing only active incidents assigned to them. Which tool builds that?
questions.explanation: The condition builder in the list filter narrows records by conditions.

questions.stem: What do tags let users do?
options: Label records so they can be found and grouped
questions.explanation: Tags are labels used to find and group records.

questions.stem: Which feature fills in several fields at once when creating a new record?
questions.explanation: A form template prefills a chosen set of field values.

questions.stem: Which tool lets an administrator drag fields onto a form visually?
questions.explanation: Form Designer is the drag-and-drop tool for form layout.

questions.stem: Incident, Problem and Change Request all extend which table?
questions.explanation: They are task-based tables that extend the Task table.

questions.stem: How does a Visual Task Board present work?
options: As cards in lanes that can be dragged between lanes
questions.explanation: A Visual Task Board shows tasks as cards you move between lanes.

questions.stem: In a notification record, which section defines the recipients?
questions.explanation: The Who will receive section sets users, groups and other recipients.

questions.stem: What must happen for an event-based notification to send?
options: The event must be registered and then fired
A catalog item must be ordered
An update set must be committed
questions.explanation: The event has to exist in the registry and be triggered, for example by a script or flow.

questions.stem: Which best describes a dashboard?
options: A page that groups reports and other visualizations
A table that stores user passwords
questions.explanation: A dashboard gathers reports and visualizations on one page.

questions.stem: Which two of these tables hold task-based records? Select two.
questions.explanation: Incident and Change Request extend Task. User and Location do not.

questions.stem: A user needs list data in a spreadsheet. What can they do from the list?
options: Export the list to a file such as CSV or Excel
questions.explanation: Lists can be exported to common file formats.

questions.stem: What does a related list on a form show?
options: Records from other tables that reference the current record
questions.explanation: Related lists display records in other tables that point to the current record.

questions.stem: Which catalog item type creates a record directly in a chosen table, such as an incident?
questions.explanation: A record producer creates a record in a specified table from a catalog form.

questions.stem: Which lets a user order several related items in one request?
questions.explanation: An order guide bundles related catalog items into one order.

questions.stem: How does a catalog item collect information from the person ordering?
questions.explanation: Catalog variables are the input fields on the item.

questions.stem: What is a variable set?
options: A reusable group of variables shared across catalog items
A set of ACLs for a table
questions.explanation: A variable set lets several items reuse the same group of variables.

questions.stem: In Knowledge Management, where are articles organized?
options: In knowledge bases, often grouped by categories
questions.explanation: Articles live in knowledge bases and are grouped by category.

questions.stem: Which article state makes an article visible to people who can read its knowledge base?
questions.explanation: Only published articles are visible to readers.

questions.stem: In Workflow Studio, what starts a flow?
questions.explanation: Every flow begins with a trigger.

questions.stem: Which Workflow Studio component is reusable logic that several flows can call?
questions.explanation: A subflow packages logic that other flows can call.

questions.stem: In Workflow Studio, which component performs a single operation such as Create Record or Send Email?
questions.explanation: An action is one reusable operation inside a flow.

questions.stem: What are the building blocks of a Virtual Agent conversation?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent conversations are built from topics.

questions.stem: In the catalog fulfillment hierarchy, which record is a child of a requested item?
questions.explanation: A request contains requested items, and each requested item can have catalog tasks.

questions.stem: What controls which users can read a knowledge base?
questions.explanation: User criteria define who may read or contribute to a knowledge base.

questions.stem: A child table that extends a parent table gets what from the parent?
questions.explanation: A child table inherits the fields of its parent.

questions.stem: Which table stores field definitions for tables (the dictionary)?
questions.explanation: sys_dictionary holds the definition of each field.

questions.stem: What does a reference field do?
options: Points to a record in another table
questions.explanation: A reference field stores a link to a record in another table.

questions.stem: Which field type stores a value picked from a predefined list?
questions.explanation: A choice field limits the value to a defined list.

questions.stem: What does an ACL control?
options: Who can read, write, create or delete data
questions.explanation: Access control rules decide who can perform operations on data.

questions.stem: When does an ACL grant access?
options: When all of its role, condition and script checks that are present pass
Only when a script is present
questions.explanation: Every check defined on the rule must evaluate to true.

questions.stem: If no ACL matches a request, what is the default outcome in a standard secure setup?
questions.explanation: The default is to deny access when no rule grants it.

questions.stem: Which role must an admin elevate to before creating or editing ACLs?
questions.explanation: Changing ACLs requires elevating to the security_admin role.

questions.stem: Where is imported data staged before it is moved to the target table?
questions.explanation: Imports land in a staging (import set) table first.

questions.stem: What does a transform map define?
options: How staging fields map to target table fields
questions.explanation: A transform map maps source fields to target fields.

questions.stem: Which transform map setting helps decide whether to update an existing record or create a new one?
questions.explanation: Coalesce fields are matched against existing records to decide update or insert.

questions.stem: What does the CMDB store?
options: Configuration items and the relationships between them
questions.explanation: The CMDB records configuration items and how they relate.

questions.stem: What is the Common Service Data Model (CSDM)?
options: A framework for modeling services and configuration items consistently in the CMDB
questions.explanation: CSDM gives a consistent way to model services and CIs.

questions.stem: Configuration item classes extend which base table?
questions.explanation: CI classes ultimately extend cmdb_ci.

questions.stem: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for configuring the roles and ACLs that protect a customer's own data?
questions.explanation: Customers configure access to their own data. The vendor secures the underlying platform.

questions.stem: What does Security Center provide?
options: A consolidated view of the instance's security posture
questions.explanation: Security Center summarizes security posture in one place.

questions.stem: What is the best practice for giving many users the same access?
options: Assign roles to a group and add the users to the group
Give each user the admin role
questions.explanation: Granting roles through groups keeps access manageable.

questions.stem: Which two are valid data source types for an import set? Select two.
questions.explanation: Files and JDBC connections are data sources. Dictionary and ACL are not.

questions.stem: Which feature can make a field read-only or mandatory on a form based on a condition, without scripting?
questions.explanation: UI policies change field behavior on a form based on conditions.

questions.stem: Where does a business rule run?
questions.explanation: Business rules are server-side logic.

questions.stem: Which business rule timing runs before the record is saved and can change field values without an extra update?
questions.explanation: A before rule runs prior to the database write, so changes are saved with the record.

questions.stem: Which client script type runs when a field's value changes on a form?
questions.explanation: An onChange client script fires when a field value changes.

questions.stem: What is an update set used for?
options: Capturing customizations so they can be moved to another instance
questions.explanation: Update sets record configuration changes so they can be moved between instances.

questions.stem: Which update set state means it has stopped collecting changes and is ready to be moved?
questions.explanation: Marking an update set Complete closes it for collection so it can be moved.

questions.stem: Which server-side API is used in scripts to query and update records?
questions.explanation: GlideRecord is the server-side API for database access.

questions.stem: Which two of these run on the server? Select two.
questions.explanation: Business rules and Script Includes are server-side. UI policies and client scripts run in the browser.

questions.stem: Which element in the banner frame lets a user search for records, knowledge and other content across the instance?
questions.explanation: Global search sits in the banner frame and searches across the instance.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Now Platform?
options: A cloud platform for building and running digital workflows on a shared data model
questions.explanation: The Now Platform is a cloud platform for digital workflows built on a common data model.

questions.stem: Which two are capabilities of the Now Platform? Select two.
questions.explanation: The platform provides workflow automation and role-based access control. The others are not platform capabilities.

questions.stem: Where in the All menu can a user quickly return to pages they visited recently?
questions.explanation: The All menu includes Favorites and History tabs. History lists recently visited pages.

questions.stem: Which program provides free Personal Developer Instances?
questions.explanation: PDIs are provided through the ServiceNow Developer Program.

questions.stem: What does the application navigator contain?
questions.explanation: The navigator lists applications and the modules inside them.

questions.stem: What happens when a user clicks a record in a list?
options: The record opens in its form
The list is converted to a report
questions.explanation: Selecting a record in a list opens it in its form.

questions.stem: What does impersonating a user let an administrator do?
options: See and test the instance as that user would
questions.explanation: Impersonation lets an admin experience the instance as another user, which helps test access.

questions.stem: Which of these appears in the banner frame?
options: The user menu and global search
questions.explanation: The banner frame holds items such as global search and the user menu.

questions.stem: What can happen to a Personal Developer Instance that goes unused for a long time?
options: It is copied to the Store
It is converted to a table
questions.explanation: Inactive PDIs may be reclaimed, so keep using them and keep copies of work you care about.

questions.stem: What is a plugin in ServiceNow?
options: A package of functionality that can be activated to add features
questions.explanation: Plugins bundle functionality that can be activated on an instance.

questions.stem: Which setting is a personal preference that affects only the user who sets it?
options: The date and time format in their own preferences
A new field on the Incident table
questions.explanation: User preferences apply to one user. The others change the platform for everyone.

questions.stem: What decides the text shown for a referenced record in a reference field?
options: The display value of the referenced table
questions.explanation: A reference field shows the display value defined on the referenced table.

questions.stem: Where is the safest place to try a new configuration before it reaches production?
options: A sub-production instance such as development
questions.explanation: Changes are normally built and tested in sub-production instances first.

questions.stem: Which interface do administrators and fulfillers typically use to configure the platform and work records?
questions.explanation: The standard platform UI is where admins and fulfillers configure and work.

questions.stem: Which tool is used to build pages for workspaces and portals in the Next Experience?
questions.explanation: UI Builder is the tool for building Next Experience pages.

questions.stem: Which two are personalizations rather than customizations? Select two.
options: Reordering columns on your own list
Adding a field to the Incident table
questions.explanation: Personalizations affect only the user. Adding a field or an ACL changes the platform for everyone.

questions.stem: How is an installed application brought up to a newer available version?
options: Import it with a transform map
questions.explanation: Application Manager shows available updates for installed applications.

questions.stem: Which statement about customizations is true?
options: They change the platform for all users and are tracked in update sets
They affect only one user and are never tracked
They cannot be moved between instances
They are only possible with an import set
questions.explanation: Customizations are shared changes that are captured in update sets so they can be moved.

questions.stem: What does the ServiceNow Store offer?
options: Certified applications and integrations from ServiceNow and partners
questions.explanation: The Store distributes certified applications and integrations.

questions.stem: In the list filter condition builder, which operator makes a record match only when both conditions are true?
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions to be true. OR requires either.

questions.stem: How can a user edit a field value directly in a list when list editing is allowed?
questions.explanation: List editing lets users double-click a cell to change the value in place.

questions.stem: Which task field is meant for notes visible only to internal fulfillers?
questions.explanation: Work notes are internal. Additional comments are visible to the customer.

questions.stem: Which feature gives different audiences different layouts of the same form?
questions.explanation: Form views let one table show different form layouts to different audiences.

questions.stem: On a task, what is the difference between Assignment group and Assigned to?
options: Assignment group is a team and Assigned to is an individual user
They are always the same field
Assigned to is a table and Assignment group is a script
Assignment group is only used for notifications
questions.explanation: Assignment group is the team responsible. Assigned to is the person working it.

questions.stem: What does the condition on a notification control?
options: Whether the notification sends when its trigger occurs
questions.explanation: The condition filters which records or events actually cause the notification to send.

questions.stem: Which report type best shows each category as a share of a whole?
questions.explanation: A pie chart shows proportions of a whole.

questions.stem: Which field setting stops a record from being saved while the field is empty?
questions.explanation: A mandatory field must have a value before the record can be saved.

questions.stem: What does the activity stream on a task form show?
options: Comments, work notes and tracked field changes
questions.explanation: The activity stream lists comments, work notes and audited field changes.

questions.stem: Who can see a tag whose visibility is set to Private?
options: Only the user who created it
questions.explanation: A private tag is visible only to its creator.

questions.stem: What does article versioning in Knowledge Management provide?
options: A history of changes as an article is edited
A copy of the table schema
questions.explanation: Versioning keeps a history of an article as it changes.

questions.stem: Which feature hides or shows a catalog variable based on another variable's value?
questions.explanation: Catalog UI policies change variable behavior on the catalog form.

questions.stem: What are catalog categories used for?
options: Organizing catalog items so users can find them
questions.explanation: Categories group catalog items to make browsing easier.

questions.stem: In Workflow Studio, what carries data from one step to a later step?
questions.explanation: Data pills reference outputs of earlier steps so later steps can use them.

questions.stem: Which trigger type starts a flow when a record is created or updated?
questions.explanation: A record trigger starts a flow on record create or update.

questions.stem: How can a flow be checked before it is activated?
options: Run it with the Test feature
Import it with a transform map
questions.explanation: Workflow Studio has a test feature for trying a flow before activating it.

questions.stem: What can a Virtual Agent conversation do when it cannot resolve the user's issue?
options: Transfer the user to a live agent
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent can hand the conversation to a live agent.

questions.stem: Which table stores requested items from the catalog?
questions.explanation: Requested items are stored in sc_req_item.

questions.stem: What does retiring a knowledge article do?
options: Takes it out of normal use so readers no longer see it
Grants admin rights to the author
questions.explanation: A retired article is no longer available to readers.

questions.stem: Which two are Workflow Studio building blocks? Select two.
questions.explanation: Flows and subflows are Workflow Studio components. ACLs and update sets are not.

questions.stem: What does the Extends table setting on a table define?
questions.explanation: Extends table names the parent the table inherits from.

questions.stem: Which tool displays how tables relate to one another?
questions.explanation: The schema map shows tables and their relationships.

questions.stem: What is a journal field used for?
options: Keeping a running log of entries such as comments and work notes
questions.explanation: Journal fields hold a series of entries, such as comments and work notes.

questions.stem: What does dot-walking let a script or condition do?
options: Reach fields on a related record through a reference field
questions.explanation: Dot-walking follows reference fields to read fields on related records.

questions.stem: An ACL named incident.priority applies to which scope?
options: The priority field on the Incident table
questions.explanation: A table.field ACL applies to that one field on that table.

questions.stem: When several ACLs could apply to a request, which are evaluated first?
questions.explanation: Evaluation starts with the most specific rules and moves to broader ones.

questions.stem: What is a group in ServiceNow?
options: A collection of users that can be given roles and assignments
questions.explanation: Groups collect users so roles and work can be assigned to them together.

questions.stem: Which CMDB capability helps identify and reconcile duplicate or conflicting CI data?
questions.explanation: The Identification and Reconciliation Engine keeps CI data consistent.

questions.stem: After data is loaded into an import set table, what moves it to the target table?
questions.explanation: The transform map moves staged rows into the target table.

questions.stem: Which practice follows least privilege?
options: Granting users only the roles they need
questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the access a person needs.

questions.stem: Which business rule timing runs in the background after the save so the user is not kept waiting?
questions.explanation: Async rules are queued and run after the save without holding up the user.

questions.stem: Which client-side call sets a field's value on a form?
questions.explanation: g_form.setValue is the client-side way to set a field on a form.

questions.stem: What is a Script Include?
options: A reusable server-side script that other scripts can call
questions.explanation: Script Includes hold reusable server-side code.

questions.stem: Which integration method lets an external system create and read records over HTTP?
questions.explanation: The REST Table API exposes tables for create, read, update and delete over HTTP.

questions.stem: What does a UI action add?
options: A button, link or menu item on a form or list
questions.explanation: UI actions add buttons, links and menu items to forms and lists.

questions.stem: What should an admin do after retrieving an update set from another instance and before committing it?
options: Preview it to check for problems
questions.explanation: Previewing finds conflicts and problems before the update set is committed.

questions.stem: How does a data policy differ from a UI policy?
options: A data policy enforces rules on the server regardless of how data is entered
A data policy only changes colors
A data policy runs only in the browser
questions.explanation: Data policies are enforced server-side, including for imports and web services.

questions.stem: How should a client script get data from the server?
questions.explanation: GlideAjax calls a server-side Script Include from the browser asynchronously.

questions.stem: In a business rule script, what does the variable current refer to?
questions.explanation: current is the record the business rule is running against.

questions.stem: Which two run in the browser? Select two.
questions.explanation: UI policies and client scripts run client-side. Business rules and Script Includes run on the server.

questions.stem: A user can open an incident form, but the Short description field shows no value. The table-level read ACL on Incident passes for this user. What is the most likely cause?
options: The incident table has no ACLs defined
A field-level read ACL on incident.short_description is denying the user
The user has not committed an update set
The CMDB is out of sync
questions.explanation: Field access needs both the table-level and the field-level ACL to pass, so a failing field ACL hides just that field.

questions.stem: Two read ACLs match the same incident record at the same level of specificity. One requires the itil role. The other requires the user to be the record caller. A user has no itil role but is the caller. What happens?
options: Access is denied because the itil ACL failed
Access is denied until an admin approves it
Access is granted because one matching ACL passed
Access is granted only if both ACLs pass
questions.explanation: When several ACLs match at the same level, passing any one of them grants access.

questions.stem: An administrator opens the ACL list and cannot create a new rule. What should they do first?
questions.explanation: Creating or editing ACLs requires elevating to security_admin.

questions.stem: An administrator writes a scripted ACL. Which variable does the script set to true to grant access?
questions.explanation: An ACL script grants access by setting the answer variable to true. current refers to the record being checked.

questions.stem: A user has the itil role only through membership in a group. The user is removed from that group. What happens?
options: The user keeps the role permanently
The user loses the role unless it is granted another way
The role is deleted from the instance
questions.explanation: Roles granted through a group last only while the user is a member.

questions.stem: A file with 500 rows was loaded into an import set table, but the target table has no new records. Which step was most likely missed?
questions.explanation: Rows stay in the staging table until a transform map moves them to the target table.

questions.stem: A transform map coalesces on the email field. An imported row has an email that matches an existing record. What happens?
questions.explanation: A coalesce match updates the existing record. With no match, a new record is inserted.

questions.stem: Which two can change data while an import is being transformed? Select two.
questions.explanation: Transform scripts and field map scripts run server-side during the transform. UI policies and client scripts run in the browser.

questions.stem: An integration user calls the REST Table API on incident with the correct endpoint but gets an access error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The integration user lacks the roles the ACLs require
Incident cannot be read over REST
The instance needs a transform map
questions.explanation: Table API requests are subject to ACLs, so the integration user needs the right roles.

questions.stem: Which record holds the endpoint URL and HTTP methods for calling an external web service from the instance?
questions.explanation: An outbound REST Message defines the endpoint and its HTTP methods.
